unresolved_added: The official task text is unavailable, so the reconstructed task boundary rests only on the paper's own framing.
The buyer-, seller-, and balance-market regimes are chosen from visual trend direction without a formal change-point test.
Political and economic state is explicitly excluded even though it can move supply, demand, and price simultaneously.
All supply-demand relationships are assumed time-invariant despite the multi-decade oil series and future projections.
Oil consumption is assumed not to affect electricity production or price, severing a central cross-energy feedback.
The differential relations are asserted rather than derived from observed market behavior or economic identities.
Demand is defined with Dmin, but the printed analytic solution uses Dmax, which is undefined in the notation table.
The barrel-to-distance conversion mixes daily oil supply with yearly travel demand and requires an explicit time conversion audit.
The fitted coefficients and integration constants are reported without uncertainty, residuals, or held-out evaluation.
Calling the SSDM reliable from one 2006 equilibrium comparison overstates a single-point reality check.
The tax rate is assumed proportional to oil price without a statutory, behavioral, or incidence model.
The tax-receipt ratio is built from equilibrium price and supply substitutions but does not model tax pass-through or taxable volume directly.
The tax sensitivity table lacks a formula, data source, parameter definition, and reproducible calculation path.
The static tax result explicitly omits tax feedback on the supply-price curve and time drift of the demand-price curve.
The base efficiency definition uses 365 days, while the HEV and CV substitutions visibly use 356, changing both reported values.
Oil stock and travel-distance projections need unit validation across thousand barrels per day, reserve stock, billion kilometers, and years.
The Fig. 3 prose says completely using CVs for both the 2020 and 2029 exhaustion dates; the second label is likely a vehicle-class error.
The exhaustion projection holds historical demand relationships and reserve accounting fixed far beyond the fitted period.
The generation-rate denominator combines working hours and installed capacity without documenting plant-level units, averaging, or losses.
Non-thermal plants are assumed to run at full load, while thermal-hour scenarios are stylized and not validated against dispatch data.
BEV and PHEV charging margins are assigned from qualitative endurance and daily-load reasoning without charging profiles or regional grids.
The 38.5% static PHEV upper bound inherits the unvalidated generation-margin and supply-demand assumptions.
The linear ODE is justified by unnamed engineers' advice rather than a derivation, local domain, or competing functional-form test.
The paper calls a1, a2, b1, and b2 vehicle-specification constants even though their interpretations include market competition and saturation.
The fitted a2=-0.0822 and b2=-4.915 contradict the subsequent validation prose that interprets a2>0 and b2>0.
The exponential solution forms and fitted coefficients are reported without the raw regression design, residuals, or parameter covariance.
The steady state requires a nonzero determinant and admissible nonnegative counts, but neither condition is checked.
The two fit plots reuse the fitting data and therefore do not provide independent validation.
The claim that trajectories approach realistic fixed values is qualitative and lacks observed long-horizon targets.
The product a0=kWSEmax is a proposed decomposition; k is undetermined and the factors are not jointly estimated.
The sensitivity plot refers to 'figure*', leaving an unresolved cross-reference.
Increasing a0 by 10%-50% is not tied to feasible changes in infrastructure, endurance, capacity, or policy cost.
The LP assumes an ideal system operating at the optimum and that one scalar environmental cost fully represents pollution.
The model mixes HEV, BEV, and PHEV assumptions before later separating their constraints, making the base vehicle boundary ambiguous.
Combined efficiency mixes heat-to-electricity and vehicle efficiency using values and symbols whose provenance and units are incomplete.
Energy-balance rows require source-sector definitions and common Quadrillion-Btu units that are not frozen in a machine-readable matrix.
Environmental costs Pij are not fully sourced, dated, or supplied with uncertainty, so the LP objective cannot be independently replayed.
The text and legend refer to restrictions No.1-No.10, but Tbl. 6 visibly lists only constraints 1-8.
Coal and renewable constraint descriptions both call the variable x11 although the formulas use x34 and x44.
Several capacity limits are described as installed capacity or drilling amount without dates, conversion factors, or geographic scope.
The unconstrained all-renewable solution is called impossible, but the subsequent constraint additions are not derived from a complete feasibility audit.
Natural gas becomes the preferred constrained source and is then rejected by an additional cap, illustrating sensitivity to ad hoc constraint ordering.
The priority order of energy sources is asserted from one environmental-cost specification and omits cost, reliability, land, and transition constraints.
The text alternates between ultimate constraints No.1-No.8 and No.1-No.10, leaving the final LP specification uncertain.
The statement that looser constraints always improve the environment is based on six plotted combinations, not a general proof.
The common critical point eta=0.85 is read from internal plots without uncertainty, grid resolution, or stability analysis.
Because PALL decreases with eta, dPALL/deta should be negative; saying the derivative 'is going down' is sign and second-derivative ambiguous.
The BEV constraint x11>=0 is explained as removing oil restriction, but it does not require zero petroleum use and may not encode the stated mechanism.
Type-specific xc and petroleum bounds are estimated from electricity margin and one vehicle example without uncertainty or fleet heterogeneity.
The type comparison uses one environmental-cost objective and does not equalize range, service, lifecycle, cost, or infrastructure burdens.
The Toyota Prius statement calls a 2007 release a PHEV and uses sales timing as validation; the factual classification and causal link are questionable.
Another unresolved 'figure*' reference appears in the external validation discussion.
The Conclusion heading contains no distinct conclusion prose before the Strengths section begins on the next page.
Claims of robustness and mutual validation are broader than the supplied single-data fits, static comparisons, and internal plots.
The authors themselves state that many coefficients are simplified or statistically estimated and some solutions are not practical or realizable.
The recommendation to increase oil tax lacks distributional, legal, behavioral, fiscal, and implementation analysis.
The generation-source ranking is reused as policy advice without uncertainty, capacity expansion cost, reliability, or lifecycle boundaries.
The claim that coal can be saved above eta=0.85 but petroleum and natural gas can never be saved is entirely model-internal and boundary-sensitive.
The manufacturer advice correctly rejects increasing conventional-car fuel consumption, but feasible changes to E100 and CHP share are not costed.
Appendix Tbl. 6 duplicates the main table label, creating ambiguous table identity.
The MATLAB appendix supplies partial frozen snippets without input files, data loading, function definitions, environment version, or run instructions.
The code uses fixed values such as neta=8 and ii=15 without loops or surrounding context, so the reported sensitivity analyses are not exactly reproducible.
No end-to-end uncertainty propagation, independent validation, frozen dataset, or reproducible decision package supports the final recommendations.
